title: La comadre
goal: Be recognised, and become somebody who comes here
culture: This is what all the other market missions were for. Going to the same stall until she knows you is not a trick for better prices — though it is that too. It is the difference between shopping in a place and living in it.

beats.es: ¡Ideay! Usted otra vez. Ya lo conozco a usted.
beats.objective: Tell her you know your way around now
beats.en: I know my way around here now.
beats.good: Ideay is the most Nicaraguan noise there is — surprise, greeting, disbelief, all of it. Ya lo conozco claims the place a little, and she will let you.

beats.es: Le guardé los mejores, mire. Desde temprano se los aparté.
beats.objective: She put them aside for you — check
beats.en: You kept them for me? That’s very kind.
beats.good: Le guardé from her, me los guardó from you: the same act from the two ends of it. Hearing one and being able to say the other is most of what fluency is.
This is the sentence you have been working towards since your first morning here. It means she knows what you buy, and you only get it by coming back.

beats.es: ¿Se los doy bien maduros, como la vez pasada?
beats.objective: Yes — that is how you like them
beats.en: That’s how I like them. Thank you.
beats.good: She asked because she remembered. Answering it is the entire point of going to the same stall, and it is worth more than the córdobas it saves.
